record.context_brief: possible failure of the vanishing conjecture for non-polynomial Hessian nilpotent series
record.original_question: Does there exist a Hessian nilpotent formal power series P(z) in C[[z]] that is not a polynomial and for which the Vanishing Conjecture fails? Equivalently, can one find a non-polynomial Hessian nilpotent formal power series over C such that the quantities Delta^m(P(z)^(m+1)) do not eventually vanish, or prove that no such example exists?

evidence.quote: One interesting question is whether or not the VC fails (as the JC does) for any HN formal power series P(z) in C[[z]] but P(z) not in C[z]? To our best knowledge, no such counterexample has been known yet.
Open Problem 5.2. Find a HN formal power series P(z) in C[[z]] but P(z) not in C[z], if there are any, such that the VC fails for P(z).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{C}[[z]] = \mathbb{C}[[z_1,\dots,z_n]]$ denote the ring of formal power series in $n$ variables over $\mathbb{C}$, and let $\Delta = \sum_{i=1}^n \partial^2/\partial z_i^2$ be the standard Laplacian. The Hessian of a formal power series $P(z) \in \mathbb{C}[[z]]$ is the matrix $\mathrm{Hess}(P) = (\partial^2 P/\partial z_i \partial z_j)_{1 \le i,j \le n}$, and $P$ is called Hessian nilpotent (HN) if $\mathrm{Hess}(P)$ is nilpotent as a matrix over $\mathbb{C}[[z]]$ (equivalently, all its eigenvalues are zero, or all coefficients of its characteristic polynomial except the leading one vanish). The Vanishing Conjecture (VC) for $P$ asserts that
$$\Delta^m\bigl(P(z)^{m+1}\bigr) = 0 \quad \text{for all sufficiently large } m \ge 1.$$

Problem. Either exhibit a Hessian nilpotent formal power series $P(z) \in \mathbb{C}[[z]] \setminus \mathbb{C}[z]$ (i.e., not a polynomial) for which the Vanishing Conjecture fails — that is, $\Delta^m(P^{m+1}) \ne 0$ for infinitely many $m$ — or prove that no such formal power series exists.
artifact.status_search_result: Search results show ongoing study of the Vanishing Conjecture for Hessian nilpotent series, including extensions to Laurent series (where counterexamples exist) and to differential operators (de Bondt's counterexample for non-constant coefficient operators). However, no source found exhibits a non-polynomial HN formal power series in $\mathbb{C}[[z]]$ for which VC fails, nor a proof that none exists. The problem appears still open.

status_evidence.claim: VC has been studied for various extensions; counterexamples exist in broader settings (Laurent series), but the original question for $\mathbb{C}[[z]]$ remains unresolved.
